title: Breastfeeding and Health Outcomes for Infants and Children
design: AHRQ systematic review of reviews and newer primary evidence
comparison: Breastfeeding exposure intensity/duration vs less or none
finding: Benefits associated with some infections, asthma and other outcomes; low-to-moderate certainty of no clear association for cognition, eczema and celiac disease. No clear universal duration threshold.
limitations: Most primary evidence observational; exposure heterogeneity; not causal proof for every endpoint.
conflicts: Complete contractor and panel disclosures pending
access: Indexed executive summary, results and discussion; Table 5 locator
authors: Patnode CD, Henrikson NB, Webber EM et al.

title: Breastfeeding during infancy and neurocognitive function in adolescence: 16-year follow-up of the PROBIT cluster-randomized trial
population: Belarus; 12,912 with neurocognitive testing in analysis
comparison: Breastfeeding promotion vs usual care; not formula assignment
finding: Adjusted verbal function +1.4 points (95% CI 0.3 to 2.5); no broad global cognitive advantage established.
limitations: Attrition, assessment measurement reliability, same PROBIT cohort; no comparison of all formula-fed vs breastfed infants.
conflicts: GD and SA NeuroTrax employees; data curation, writing/review roles; no formula industry support identified in checked disclosure
authors: Yang S, Martin RM, Oken E et al.

title: Breastfeeding and child cognitive development: new evidence from a large randomized trial
finding: Reported cognitive advantages, particularly verbal outcomes; later follow-up shows smaller effects.
limitations: Not independent replication of P2-02; measurement and assessor bias; numerical extraction pending.

title: Is breast truly best? Estimating the effects of breastfeeding on long-term child health and wellbeing in the United States using sibling comparisons
comparison: Differently fed siblings vs between-family comparisons
finding: 10/11 outcomes favored breastfeeding in standard models; all but one lost statistical significance in within-family models.
limitations: Within-family confounding and measurement error remain; does not negate short-term infection benefits; compare with P2-05 due shared NLSY source.
cohort: NLSY family dataset; overlap with P2-05 possible

title: Effect of breast feeding on intelligence in children: prospective study, sibling pairs analysis, and meta-analysis
design: Observational prospective and sibling analysis plus meta-analysis
finding: Maternal IQ strongly predicted breastfeeding and accounted for much apparent association.
limitations: Residual confounding; NLSY lineage may overlap P2-04.
funding: Wellcome fellowship noted in author affiliation; study-level grants unverified
authors: Der G, Batty GD, Deary IJ

title: Human milk composition: nutrients and bioactive factors
comparison: Composition across lactation; no randomized formula comparison
finding: Human milk contains dynamic nutrients, immune factors and bioactive constituents.
limitations: Composition does not prove clinical superiority for every long-term outcome.
access: Indexed bibliographic identity; quantitative composition extraction pending

title: Conduct and reporting of formula milk trials: systematic review
finding: 100/125 high risk of bias, 5/125 low; 98/117 reporting funding industry-supported; 87/112 reporting COI had industry-related author COI; favorable conclusions associated with high RoB OR 7.58 (1.95–29.46).
limitations: Not every trial invalid; review does not establish harms of regulated formula; outcome and review funding separate; 2021 correction n2890 needs inspection.
funding: Imperial Health Charity; no role in design/analysis/writing/decision per authors
conflicts: Lead author outside-work fees including DBV, Prota, Cochrane, expert witness work involving formula claims, and public health committee roles; other disclosures require full extraction
publication_integrity: Correction doi:10.1136/bmj.n2890 identified; correction contents not independently extracted

title: Health and nutrition claims for infant formula: international cross sectional survey
finding: 1884 claims; 161/608 products with claims cited references; 28/32 registered trials industry-funded and/or industry-affiliated authors.
limitations: Product snapshot not current recall or composition list; not clinical efficacy trial; full author disclosure extraction pending.
access: Indexed original results and funding statement

title: Effects of Infant Formula With Human Milk Oligosaccharides on Growth and Morbidity: A Randomized Multicenter Trial
comparison: 1 g/L 2'FL + .5 g/L LNnT vs identical base formula without these HMOs
followup: Formula to 6 months, outcomes through 12 months
finding: Growth/tolerance primary context; parent-reported bronchitis 10.2% vs 27.6% through 12 months; antibiotics 42.0% vs 60.9%.
limitations: Secondary outcomes, multiple comparisons and parent report; no equivalence to breast milk; independent replication needed.
funding: Nestlé grants and nonfinancial support to participating hospitals
conflicts: Several current/former Nestlé employees; GP/CC other sponsored studies
access: PMC original affiliations and disclosure, indexed results
adverse_events: Secondary morbidity/adverse-event clusters reported; comprehensive SAE and denominators extraction pending

title: Long chain polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation in infants born at term
comparison: Added LCPUFA vs no added LCPUFA
finding: No consistent neurodevelopmental benefit supporting routine addition in reviewed trials.
limitations: Older formulations; no conclusion that DHA is biologically unnecessary or current regulatory standards should change.

title: Infant formula supplementation with long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids has no effect on Bayley developmental scores at 18 months of age--IPD meta-analysis of 4 large clinical trials
population: Term and preterm infants in four trials
finding: Mental developmental index MD -0.8 (-2.8 to 1.2); psychomotor MD -1.0 (-2.7 to 0.7).
limitations: Mixed term/preterm; review overlap with P2-10 requires matching; not all contemporary formulations.

title: Hydrolysed formula and risk of allergic or autoimmune disease: systematic review and meta-analysis
population: Infants at risk or general populations, trial-specific
comparison: Hydrolysed vs other formula or breastfeeding comparison
finding: No consistent prevention benefit; excluded Chandra studies implicated in research integrity concerns.
limitations: Prevention distinct from treatment of diagnosed allergy; full trial funding and notice reconciliation pending.

title: Does a profound change in toilet-training affect development of bowel and bladder control?
finding: Median training onset 13 months later; bowel control 16 months later; day/night bladder control not affected according to authors.
limitations: Different caregiving methods; no random assignment to diaper type; authors distinguish maternal control vs child initiative; not US national trend.
authors: Largo RH, Molinari L, von Siebenthal K, Wolfensberger U

title: Effects of Early Toilet Training and Elimination Communication With Respect to Diaper Types
population: Caregivers reporting diaper and training patterns
finding: More diaper-free time associated with earlier toilet training, enhanced by cloth use; cloth not associated with rash/balm use; more diaper-free time associated with reduced caregiver continuous sleep.
limitations: Self-selection, reverse causation, recall bias, unknown endpoint definitions/adjustment; sample and adjusted effect extraction pending.

title: Measuring the impact of disposable diapers on urination elimination signals in non-toilet-trained children
finding: Within-child observation using moisture sensor and cue assessment.
limitations: Treat as linked to P2-16 until cohort identity established; not a separate replication.
cohort: Antwerp crossover pilot; link to P2-16 provisional

title: Do disposable diapers reduce urination elimination signals in non-toilet-trained children?
finding: Verbal cues 43% vs 13%; seeking caregiver contact 52% vs 13%; leg movement and activity cessation each 87% vs 35%; genital attention during urination 78% vs 13%.
limitations: Small sample, incomplete cases, repeated paired outcomes; no long-term training age; do not reconstruct matched counts or calculate independent RR.
funding: Full final-paper disclosure pending; related methods paper reports no specific grant, not proof for this report
cohort: Antwerp crossover pilot; probable shared lineage

title: Assisted infant toilet training and the prevalence of functional gastrointestinal disorders up to the age of 9 months: a randomised, controlled trial
design: Randomized controlled trial, first BABITT report (online 2025)
population: 271 infants, median 34 days; 136 vs 135 assigned; complete cases 127 vs 132
comparison: Early assisted infant toilet training vs delayed start
finding: Composite functional GI disorder prevalence 52.0% vs 49.6%; difference +2.4 percentage points (95% CI -9.8 to 14.7).
limitations: Caregiver reported; moderate practice frequency; early GI outcome not independent toileting or later bladder health; later follow-up planned.
funding: Region Dalarna, Regional Research Council Uppsala–Örebro, Mayflower Association, Samaritan Foundation, Swedish Enuresis Academy; authors state no funder role

title: Bowel and bladder function in infant toilet training (BABITT) - protocol for a randomized, two-armed intervention study
comparison: Early vs later assisted toilet training
finding: Defines study rationale; no efficacy outcome.
limitations: Do not count as clinical results; later bladder outcomes not established in current extraction.
funding: See BABITT funding; protocol-specific verification pending

title: Assisted Infant Toilet Training and Bladder and Bowel Health: A Global Integrative Review
comparison: Assisted training vs varying conventional practices
finding: Suggestive observational benefits and serious bias limitations; no definitive prevention claim.
limitations: Review overlap with historical/cultural studies pending.
funding: CAUL/member institutions open-access support as recorded in Stage 1; project grant disclosure to recheck
conflicts: No declared COI per Stage 1 extraction; recheck full text
access: Inherited Stage 1 publisher extraction; not re-read this pass

title: Urinary bladder control during the first 3 years of life in healthy children in Vietnam--a comparison study with Swedish children
population: 47 Vietnamese children with Swedish reference comparison
comparison: Early caregiver-assisted training vs historical Swedish practices
finding: Early toileting routine and different bladder development observations; 81% of mothers began at 3 months in earlier linked report; all regularly potty trained at 12 months.
limitations: Caregiver-assisted routine not autonomous continence; culture, cohort, design differences; no causal inference.

title: Does the development and use of modern disposable diapers affect bladder control? A systematic review
population: Diaper use and bladder control studies
finding: Relevant review; cannot assign causal estimate until eligible study results and bias extracted.
limitations: Stage 1 flagged possible commercial involvement but sponsor not verified; do not name a company or infer misconduct.
funding: Unknown; source-level sponsor role not verified

title: Relationship between age at initiation of toilet training and duration of training: a prospective study
finding: Earlier starts associated with longer training duration in published literature; exact estimates pending.
limitations: No randomized diaper comparison; readiness and family factors.
authors: Blum NJ, Taubman B, Nemeth N

title: Disposable nappies for preventing napkin dermatitis in infants
finding: Insufficient high-quality randomized evidence for prevention superiority.
limitations: Old search through 2004; one cloth arm not adequately randomized; newer products not assessed.

title: Increased carrying reduces infant crying: a randomized controlled trial
finding: 1.23 vs 2.16 hours/day crying/fussing; 43% less in trial.
limitations: Old trial, subjective outcomes; carrying does not imply safe sleep in a carrier; newer replication and harms pending.

title: Five-year follow-up of harms and benefits of behavioral infant sleep intervention: randomized trial
population: Children in infant behavioral sleep intervention trial
finding: No marked lasting benefit or harm detected in measured outcomes.
limitations: Not proof every method is safe, especially newborns or medically vulnerable infants; attrition and precision need full extraction.
conflicts: Authors report no relevant financial relationships in prior 3 years or other influencing activities

title: Massage for promoting mental and physical health in typically developing infants under the age of six months
finding: Evidence poor quality; no robust broad developmental claim.
limitations: Version lineage 2022 listing requires verification; no extrapolation to preterm infants or oils.
access: Indexed original review abstract and text
authors: Bennett C, Underdown A, Barlow J

title: Disposable and reusable nappies in the UK: life cycle assessment
finding: Relevant historical reference; later 2023 Defra assessment compares 18 impact categories; no universal winner stated in 2025 parliamentary response.
limitations: Not US household cost or health study; assumptions washing, drying, reuse and energy mix matter.

title: Choosing an Infant Formula
comparison: Regulated age-appropriate formula vs unsafe homemade substitutes
finding: FDA regulates nutrient and safety minimums; homemade formula unsafe.
limitations: Not product-specific proof of equivalence or no risks; specific age/medical indication matters.

title: Infant Formula Preparation and Storage
finding: Powder is not sterile; correct label ratio and special precautions for vulnerable babies.
limitations: No generic preparation override; follow current local guidance and medical plan.

title: CPSC Approves New Federal Safety Standard for Infant Sling Carriers
finding: Suffocation/fall hazards; keep airway visible and unobstructed, chin away from chest.
limitations: Not efficacy evidence or current model recall clearance; safe sleep separate.

title: Healthy Habits: Diaper Changing at Home
finding: Includes both diaper types; hygiene and prompt changing remain important.
limitations: Not comparative effectiveness evidence.

title: Infant and young child feeding
finding: Exclusive breastfeeding for first 6 months, complementary foods from around 6 months and continued breastfeeding to 2 years or beyond as feasible.
limitations: Population guidance; adequate nutrition and individual circumstances matter; no coercion.
conflicts: Panel and underlying evidence disclosures pending

title: Nutrient specifications, 21 CFR 107.100
finding: Per 100 kcal as prepared; regulatory adequacy separate from extra benefit claims.
limitations: FDA official guidance cross-reference; no brand-specific guarantee.

title: Infant Formula Guidance Documents & Regulatory Information
finding: Regulatory nutrient and manufacturing requirements; check current recalls and exact labels separately.
limitations: Not clinical superiority evidence.
